memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'You will perish among the nations; the land of your enemies will devour
you. Those of you who are left will waste away in the lands of their
enemies because of their sins; also because of their ancestors' sins they
will waste away'" - Lev 26:38-39 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The warning section reaches its lowest point. The people waste away in
foreign lands, far from home, bearing the weight of sin. It is a picture
of utter desolation — life draining away in exile, everything lost.

We have followed this chapter down a long and darkening road, and here it
touches the bottom. And yet — this is not where the chapter ends. Keep
that firmly in mind as we read these heavy words. The very next verse turns
a corner none of the exiles could have engineered for themselves.

Dear reader, this bottom point is important precisely because of what
follows. Often it is only when a person reaches the end of themselves that
they finally turn back to God. The prodigal son did not come to his senses
in the middle of his spending spree. He came to his senses in the pig pen,
at the bottom, with nothing left (Luke 15:17).

There is a mercy in reaching the end of the far country. As long as we
have something left to trust in — our own strength, our own resources, our
own plans — we tend to keep leaning on it. Sometimes God allows us to come
to the very end so that we will finally look up.

If you feel you have wasted away, that everything is lost, that you are as
far from home as you can be — do not despair. That is often exactly where
grace begins. The next verse is coming. Do not stop reading the story of
your life at the pig pen.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I reached the end of myself in some area of life?
2. Am I still leaning on my own resources rather than turning to God?
3. Could my lowest point be the very place grace begins?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, when I reach the end of myself, let it be the place I turn back to
You. Even in my lowest moments, remind me that the next verse of grace is
coming. Amen.
